Summary: SOL-01 Record validated hourly solar generation
Description:
As a prosumer, I want validated hourly meter readings recorded so that my generated energy can be credited.

Acceptance criteria
An authenticated meter submits a household ID, timestamp and non-negative kWh value. A valid reading is stored once. A duplicate meter/timestamp does not add credits twice. Invalid identities, missing fields and negative readings are rejected without changing balances.

Backlog group: Meter ingestion
Traceability: FR-001 / NFR-001
Dependencies: None
Estimate: 5 story points.
Planning reference: SOL-01. Jira assigns its own key.

Summary: SOL-02 View my available solar credit balance
Description:
As a resident, I want to view my available balance so that I know how many credits I can transfer.

Acceptance criteria
An authenticated resident sees the balance derived from committed ledger entries. A zero balance displays zero. Requests for another resident are denied. An account with 120 credits shows 120 after the page refreshes.

Backlog group: Resident credits
Traceability: FR-002 / NFR-002
Dependencies: SOL-01
Estimate: 3 story points.
Planning reference: SOL-02. Jira assigns its own key.

Summary: SOL-03 Transfer credits with validation and audit
Description:
As a resident, I want to transfer credits to a valid neighbor so that surplus generation benefits their account.

Acceptance criteria
For sender balance 120, transferring 30 yields sender 90 and recipient increase 30. Invalid recipients, zero or negative amounts and amounts above the balance are rejected. Concurrent requests cannot overspend. Sender debit, recipient credit, audit record and pending billing event commit atomically. A replayed request ID cannot duplicate a transfer.

Backlog group: Resident credits
Traceability: FR-001 / FR-003 / NFR-002
Dependencies: SOL-02
Estimate: 5 story points.
Planning reference: SOL-03. Jira assigns its own key.

Summary: SOL-04 Apply credits to utility billing
Description:
As a recipient, I want accepted credits applied to my utility statement so that my monthly bill reflects the offset.

Acceptance criteria
An accepted transfer creates one billing event. A utility acknowledgement marks it applied. A transient failure retains it for retry. A repeated delivery with the same idempotency key creates only one offset. The displayed status matches the acknowledgement.

Traceability: FR-004

Estimate: 5 story points.

Acceptance criteria
A manager selects a month and sees all three categories. Totals match a seeded dataset and exclude records outside that month. Resident-only accounts cannot open community reports. An empty month displays zero totals.

Summary: SOL-07 Manage resident and manager permissions
Description:
As a co-op administrator, I want resident and manager permissions enforced so that private account data stays restricted.

Acceptance criteria
Authorized administrators can assign or revoke a manager role. Residents cannot change their own role. Revoked permissions take effect on subsequent requests. A resident cannot read another account by changing an identifier.
